NSAIDs inhibit platelet aggregation and may thereby enhance the effect of the anticoagulant. In some settings, the risk of bleeding has been shown to increase (for example in the RE-LY study, where the risk of bleeding with dabigatran increased by 50 % when an NSAID was given concomitantly). In other settings (for direct factor Xa inhibitors), no clinically relevant increase in bleeding time has been observed in clinical studies. In epidemiological studies, the risk has been increased with the use of NSAIDs together with all types of direct-acting oral anticoagulants (DOACs). For example, a Danish cohort study found a twofold to fourfold increase in the risk of all types of bleeding leading to hospital admission (intracranial, gastrointestinal, thoracic/respiratory tract, and urinary tract) when NSAIDs were used together with DOACs, compared with DOAC use alone. The increase in risk was lowest for ibuprofen and highest for naproxen. The increase in risk corresponded to one additional bleed for every 36 years of treatment with NSAIDs.

Antiplatelet drugs inhibit platelet aggregation and may thereby enhance the effect of the anticoagulant. In some settings, the risk of bleeding has been shown to increase (for example for dabigatran in the RE-LY study). In other settings (for direct factor Xa inhibitors), no clinically relevant increase in bleeding time has been observed. Despite this, it is reasonable to recommend the same degree of caution when combining with antiplatelet drugs, including acetylsalicylic acid, for both direct thrombin inhibitors and direct factor Xa inhibitors. In the summary of product characteristics for Eliquis, concomitant use of the most potent antiplatelet drugs, such as clopidogrel, prasugrel and ticagrelor, is contraindicated. The summary of product characteristics for Zontivity states that concomitant use with oral anticoagulants should be avoided. In patients who have recently undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or recently had a stent inserted, and who also have atrial fibrillation or venous thromboembolism, combination treatment will be indicated.
